To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the optimal VaR constraint is nonconcave, (ii) the optimal portfolio is not a constant proportion of the risky asset, (iii) the optimal VaRs are not constant, and (iv) the optimal VaRS are not linear functions of the risk aversion coefficient.

the VaR-constrained optimal portfolio is nonconcave in wealth, that the VaR constraint is binding, and that the optimal portfolio is more conservative than the optimal portfolio without the VaR constraint.

the value-at-risk (V@R) of the equity holders’ wealth, as a measure of the downside risk of the life insurance contract, is a convex function of the investment rate, and that the V@R of the life insurance equity holder’s wealth can be used to derive the optimal investment rate of the life insurance company, which is a concave function of the investment horizon.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the optimal portfolio choice of an investor who is subject to a value-at-risk constraint on his portfolio.
the optimal investment and reinsurance strategies of a life insurance company.
the optimal portfolio choice for an investor with a VaR constraint.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the VaR is a good tool to measure the risk of a portfolio of assets.
the value-at-risk is a useful measure of risk, but that it has some limitations, and it is not suitable for all purposes.
the VaR model is an excellent risk management tool, but it is not a substitute for the traditional methods of measuring and controlling risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided an analytical solution of the optimal investment problem of the equity holder in a life insurance contract under the constraint that the value-at-risk of the equity holders' investment portfolio does not exceed a given level.
we have developed a new methodology that is capable of handling a large variety of problems in stochastic optimal control.
we have provided a framework for the analysis of nonconcave optimal portfolio problems with value at risk constraints.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, under the VaR constraint, the equity holders' optimal portfolio problem is not concave and hence the classical dynamic programming principle is not applicable.
the optimal investment policy is characterized by an upper bound on the proportion of the wealth invested in the risky asset and a lower bound on the proportion invested in the default-free bond.
the value of a participating life-insurance contract is sensitive to the choice of the value-at-risk (VAR) constraint.
